note: Description taken from Holmgren's 1910 original description of Eutermes brevioculatus (in German), including the alate, soldier and worker; type localities Coxipó and Cuyabá, Mato Grosso, Brazil, and Estancia Postillon, Paraguay. The figures for alate body length without wings and for the worker measurements are scrambled in the OCR, so only the legible parts are cited. The original is in German and the BHL scan OCR is only moderate: decimal points are often misread as commas or colons and some measurement digits are blurred; blurred values are not cited. The species was then placed in Eutermes and is now in Nasutitermes.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate has relatively small compound eyes and small ocelli farther from the compound eyes (about more than one diameter), which gives the species its name; the soldier nasus points slightly upwards, the vertex and nasus are not on the same outline, the head capsule is smooth with bristles only on the vertex and at the base of the nasus; Holmgren considers this species to be the E. Rippertii (Ramb.) Wasm. recorded by Silvestri 1903.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule brown to reddish brown, the postclypeus, labrum, mandible bases and antennae rusty yellow; thoracic and abdominal tergites rusty yellow to rusty brown, sternites and legs paler, wings yellowish grey. Whole body densely covered with bristles. Head broadly oval; compound eyes relatively small; ocelli rather small, the distance from the compound eyes slightly greater than their diameter; frontal marks very small, triangular; the muscle scars at the transverse band form a broad arc in front of the frontal marks. Antennae 15-segmented. Pronotum anterior margin straight with a small median notch, anterior corners rounded and blunt and sloping down, lateral margins strongly narrowing posteriorly; media close to the cubitus, with 2—3 apical branches; cubitus with 12—13 branches, the inner 5—7 coarser. Measurements: body length (with wings) 15.2 mm, without wings about 8.5 mm; head length 1.62 mm; head width 1.35 mm; from the anterior margin of the transverse band to the occiput 1.03 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule chestnut-brown, nasus reddish brown and darker, paler around the antennal bases; body rusty yellow to rusty brown, legs rusty yellow to straw-yellow. Head capsule smooth, with bristles only on the vertex and at the base of the nasus; abdominal tergites almost completely smooth (microscopic hairs visible only under the microscope), with a marginal bristle row; sternites hairy and bristled. Frontal outline with a weak elevation at the base of the nasus, nasus slightly upturned, not on the same outline as the vertex. Antennae 12 or 13-segmented. Anterior lobe of the pronotum strongly upturned, almost perpendicular to the posterior lobe, anterior margin not concave. Measurements: body length 4.9 mm; head length 1.55—1.80 mm (modal class 1.65—1.70 mm); head width 1.05—1.20 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head brown, the head capsule sutures, anterior corners of the transverse band, region around the antennae, antennae, postclypeus, labrum and the rest of the body straw-yellow to rusty yellow. Head densely bristled, abdominal plates also hairy, sternites with a marginal bristle row. Head shape as usual; frontal marks elongate (triangular), not sharply delimited from the sagittal suture; postclypeus almost as long as half its width; mandibular bare process rather large. Antennae 14-segmented. Anterior margin of the pronotum only weakly concave (the body measurements are blurred in the OCR and are not cited).
